QUESTION
 How do I export and import private keys between the same or different Hardware Security Module (HSM) enabled IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance? ANSWER
HSM-enabled DataPower appliances support the export of private keys using the crypto-export command. For key export to work, various conditions must be met: 

 * HSMs must be initialized and in the same key sharing domain on exporting and importing machines 
 * The private key in question must be marked exportable at keygen time (see keygen's exportable option) 
 * HSMs on exporting and importing machines must share internal key-wrapping keys (see hsm-clone-kwk command). A key-wrapping key is a key that encrypts another key. Each HSM has a special key inside of it, the key-wrapping key, that is used to encrypt exported private keys (and to decrypt imported private keys).

Finally, before the crypto-export crypto-import sequence, the key-wrapping keys must be synchronized using the hsm-clone-kwk command. This command must be run four times: once on the source HSM appliance (with the key-wrapping key you are copying), once on the destination HSM appliance, once again on the source HSM appliance, and once again on the destination HSM appliance. Each time the command is run, it will need the output file from the previous step (as the input to the current step) which must be moved manually (usually with the copy command). Once all of this has been done, then private keys may move from system to system with crypto-export and crypto-import. Note that the non-HSM appliance can export keys immediately at keygen time, but never at a later time. For additional information refer to the online Info Center [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/wsdatap/v3r8m2/index.jsp?topic=%2Fxi50%2Fwelcome.htm] and search for "PIN entry device".

* HSMs must be initialized and in the same key sharing domain on exporting and importing machines.

To determine when to use conversation sharing in DataPower MQ queue managers, consider the following information. 

In current versions of the DataPower firmware, the sharing conversations setting of 1 is treated as 0 when negotiating with the MQ server. There are three use cases to configure Sharing Conversations in DataPower mq-qm object: 

Case #1: The negotiated sharing conversations value is 0. This mode is similar to WebSphere MQ V6 and does not use features such as Administrator stop-quiesce, Heartbeating, Read ahead, and Client asynchronous consume. To disable sharing conversations, set a value of 0 or 1 on the Sharing Conversations attribute of the mq-qm object in DataPower, regardless of the IBM WebSphere MQ SVRCONN setting.

Case #2: The negotiated sharing conversations value is 1. This supports IBM WebSphere MQ V7 and later release features, with each TCP/IP channel instance having a single conversation. To configure this, set a value of 1 on the Sharing Conversations attribute and select "on" in the Share Single Conversation attribute of the mq-qm object in DataPower. The Share Single Conversation attribute is only visible when "Sharing Conversations" is configured with a value of "1" and then the <RETURN> key is entered. Also, set a value of 1 on the IBM WebSphere MQ SVRCONN setting.

Case #3: The negotiated sharing conversations value is 2 or more. This supports IBM WebSphere MQ 7 and later release features, with each TCP/IP channel instance supporting 2 or more conversations.

When mixed message sizes are used by the same mq-qm object, using Case #2 will benefit the mq-qm object as it will use the new buffer management feature of IBM WebSphere MQ Version 7 when making the MQGET API call. However, for DataPower firmware releases 7.0.0.x, 7.1.0.x, 7.2.0.x, and earlier, it is recommended to follow Case #1 and use a negotiated sharing conversations value of 0.

The default setting of sharing conversations (SHARECNV) value is zero in the DataPower mq-qm object, while the default value for the MQ SVRCONN channel is 10. The sharing conversations value is negotiated between the MQ server and DataPower, and the lower value takes effect.

In summary, use conversation sharing in DataPower MQ queue managers when you need to support IBM WebSphere MQ V7 and later release features, and consider the specific use case that applies to your configuration. For DataPower firmware releases 7.0.0.x, 7.1.0.x, 7.2.0.x, and earlier, use a negotiated sharing conversations value of 0. For later releases, consider using a negotiated sharing conversations value of 1, especially when mixed message sizes are used by the same mq-qm object.
